clue.text: Career stopper for tumbler on the roof

parts.note: a tumbler is a flat-bottomed drinking glass
the ceiling is the inside face of the roof over a room

explanation.surface: An acrobat's tumble off a rooftop ends their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumbler' suggests an acrobat, but it is the drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the invisible barrier that blocks women and minorities from promotion to top jobs.

clue.text: Strive to achieve something when fog lifts, or it comes down later

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word makes it read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Waiting for the fog to clear before making an attempt, or for it to fall again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes down later' tells you the second piece follows the first further down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The exhortation means make a determined attempt, going all out for a goal.

clue.text: One including a notice on my school

indicators.note: a word including something holds it within itself, so the notice goes inside 'One'

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of cards
a notice is an advertisement, shortened to ad
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil pins a notice about themselves on the school board.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a type of secondary school or place of specialist training.

clue.text: Lad with badges damaged on bicycle

definitions.note: describes where the answer is found rather than naming it

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy's badges get damaged when he falls off his bike.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it names the thing by its position, slung on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddlebag is a pouch strapped behind or beneath a bicycle saddle for carrying belongings.

clue.text: What bookies might offer at evensong?

indicators.note: the answer sits at the very start of the following word, inside it

parts.note: the first five letters of the church service

explanation.surface: A joke about betting odds being offered during an evening church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money odds, where the stake is matched by the winnings, are a price bookmakers quote.

clue.text: Support function, which can be tiring

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a synonym

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
to function is to work

explanation.surface: A support role at work can be exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a support job; it splits into two pieces and a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Legwork is the tedious running about and groundwork a task needs, which wears a person out.

clue.text: Always no work around North Street

indicators.note: the outer words wrap themselves about the following abbreviations

parts.note: taken as written
op, short for opus, is a musical work
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Nobody ever does any work around North Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the standard crossword word for a piece of work; 'no work' together forms the outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonstop means continuously, without pausing, so it can stand for always in an informal sense.

clue.text: Put up with delaying domestic work

parts.note: to put someone up is to house them
keeping someone is delaying them, as in 'what kept you?'

explanation.surface: Tolerating someone who keeps putting off the chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as one phrase meaning tolerate, but 'with' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Housekeeping is the running of a home: cleaning, cooking and managing the household chores.

clue.text: Discontinued playing cards without preparation

parts.note: a discontinued item is off the menu
the cards a player holds are a hand

explanation.surface: A card game is called off without any warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhand remarks are made on the spur of the moment, impromptu and unrehearsed.

clue.text: Defective in genes, but they stay on the rails!

indicators.note: something defective is faulty, so these letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People with faulty genes still manage to keep on the straight and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay on the rails' suggests behaving well; here it is literal, about locomotives on track.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway locomotives are called engines, and they run along the tracks or rails.

clue.text: Suffers little internally with our Chinese dish

indicators.note: something held internally sits within the word before it

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it
wee is Scottish for small
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suffering a little indigestion after a Chinese meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffers' means tolerates here, not feels pain; 'little' is the Scots word for small that slips inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet-and-sour is a sauce or dish of Chinese cuisine mixing sugar and vinegar flavours.

clue.text: Bizarre rights concealed by Sue and Al

indicators.note: something concealed is tucked away inside whatever is hiding it

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right, doubled for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people strangely hiding their legal rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes something dreamlike and strange, after the Surrealist art movement.

clue.text: Make sortie round hospital in nightdress

indicators.note: the outer word goes round the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone dashing out on a raid around the hospital wearing nightclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortie is a short nightgown or pair of pyjamas, cut above the knee.

clue.text: Girl seen in park at Hyde

indicators.note: the answer can be seen sitting inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A girl spotted in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is a large park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathy is a female first name, and crosswords often define names simply as girl or boy.

clue.text: Bans marijuana where accidents could happen

parts.note: to black something is to boycott or ban it
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A ban on cannabis, with a hint at stoned driving.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a black spot is a stretch of road known for frequent crashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A black spot is a dangerous place on a road where many crashes have occurred.

clue.text: It's Hecate, disorientated but still able to appreciate beauty

indicators.note: someone disorientated has lost their bearings, so the letters are thrown into confusion

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The Greek goddess of witchcraft is confused yet retains her artistic sensibility.
explanation.walkthrough: Hecate is a Greek goddess of magic and crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthetic person is sensitive to art and beauty, having refined taste.

clue.text: Short chats introducing former husband to converts

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to convert something is to change it

explanation.surface: Brief conversations introducing an ex to religious converts.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanges are brief conversations or swaps of remarks between people.

clue.text: Inside scar was horrible, but cleaner

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: all but the first letter of the first word and the whole second
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A wound that looked awful but was clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A car wash is a facility for cleaning vehicles, so it can be called a cleaner.

clue.text: A combination of teeth?

parts.note: surface reading: a set or mix of teeth in a mouth
setter's reading: a mixture, specifically the alloy dentists use for fillings

explanation.walkthrough: The word means any blend, and is also the mercury alloy once standard for filling teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or blend, and dental amalgam is the silver filling material for teeth.

clue.text: Boxer Mike, inquisitive to a T when making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: nosy means prying
the letter itself

explanation.surface: A former champion boxer, nosy down to the last detail, attempts a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a T' looks like the idiom for exactly; here it adds the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson is the American former world heavyweight boxing champion.

clue.text: Place for experiments, like tax on sex

parts.note: to tax someone is to test or strain them
to bed someone is to have sex with them

explanation.surface: A cheeky proposal to levy a tax on sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A test-bed is equipment or a setting for trying out new machinery or ideas under trial.

clue.text: Prospect of fuss on miniature railway

parts.note: to make a scene is to make a fuss
RY is a short form of railway

explanation.surface: Fears of a commotion on a model railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a view of the landscape, which is what scenery is.

clue.text: "Encroachment", said Ron inaccurately

definitions.note: the answer is plural, usually in the phrase make inroads

indicators.note: something said inaccurately is garbled, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ron gets a word wrong when quoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances into territory or intrusions on something, which is encroachment.

clue.text: Line of type about cashiers

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: to cashier someone is to dismiss them, so cashiers means fires

explanation.surface: A line of text written about bank tellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashiers' looks like the noun for bank staff, but it is the verb meaning sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a letter's main line in many typefaces.

clue.text: Entertainer shows old Nazi leader round Duck Street

indicators.note: the name is placed round the following letters, enclosing them

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A performer shows a former Nazi around a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostess entertains guests, receiving and looking after them at a party or event.

clue.text: Film star Stewart portrays King George with rage

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of King George
rage is extreme anger

explanation.surface: An actor plays King George in a furious rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewart Granger was a British-born Hollywood leading man of the 1940s and 1950s.

clue.text: This arrangement puts gold on the counter

parts.note: a table or counter is a flat surface
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper laying gold on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places gold after the counter in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque grouping of people or objects, a staged arrangement or scene.

clue.text: Day chef's meal put together with embarrassment

indicators.note: putting things together means assembling them, here building the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A daytime cook sheepishly presents a hastily assembled meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefacedly means in an abashed, sheepish manner, showing that one feels ashamed.
